transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?
I guess… what finally made me come in is I’ve been having some mornings where I think it might be easier if I just didn’t wake up. I don’t have a plan to hurt myself, but it scared me.
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?
Yeah… I suppose I have. Not every minute, but… more than I’d like.
Have you felt this down most days for the past two years?
No… not two years. It’s more like about a month, I think. Since my sister died unexpectedly.
Since your sister died, have you been blaming yourself or feeling guilty about her death?
Yes… I do, some. I keep thinking I should’ve called her more, or listened better. Maybe done something useful. I know, logically, I probably couldn’t have changed it, but… I still go over it.
Since your sister died, have you lost interest in things you usually enjoy?

Yes… some. I still go to book club, and the dance night, but I don’t really feel there. It’s like I’m just sitting through it. Even my garden, or cooking for the neighbors… it doesn’t give me the same little bit of happiness it used to.
Since your sister died, have you found yourself intensely longing for her or preoccupied with missing her?
I… I don’t know if I’d call it intense. I miss her, of course. But I’m not sure it’s like that, exactly.
When you feel down lately, is it mostly when you’re thinking about your sister?
I’m not really sure. Sometimes it is, I guess… but I haven’t paid close attention to whether it’s mostly that.
Even when you’re not thinking about your sister, do you still feel down?
I’m not sure. I mean… I suppose sometimes I just feel low and I’m not really thinking about anything in particular. But I haven’t really sorted it out like that.
Over the past month, have you felt down even at times when you were not thinking about your sister?
I’m not sure… I haven’t really kept track of it that way. I think there are times I feel low and I’m not especially thinking about her, but… I don’t know.
During the past month, have there been whole days when you felt down most of the day even when you were not thinking about your sister?
I don’t really know. Whole days… I haven’t been keeping track like that. There are low stretches, but I can’t say for sure.
Since your sister died, have you been feeling especially nervous or anxious?
I don’t know… I mean, I’ve felt unsettled at times, I suppose, but I wouldn’t really know if I’d call it especially anxious.
When you feel down lately, does it usually come on when something reminds you of your sister?
I’m not really sure. Sometimes it does, I suppose… but I haven’t noticed a clear pattern.
In the past month, have you felt down for most of the day on nearly every day?
I’m not sure… nearly every day sounds hard to say. I’ve had some down days, but I haven’t really kept track of whether it was most of the day.
When you start feeling down, is it usually after something reminds you of your sister?
I don’t really know. Sometimes something will remind me of her, but I can’t say that’s usually what starts it.
Over the past month, have you been waking up much earlier than usual and unable to get back to sleep?
Yes… I have been waking up early. Before dawn sometimes. I’ll sleep in pieces, and then my mind starts going, and I can’t really settle back down.
Over the past month, have you noticed your appetite has changed?
A little, yes. Food just… doesn’t really appeal much. I’ll make toast or maybe soup, and then later realize I haven’t eaten much all day. I’m not trying to lose weight.
When you feel down lately, does it happen even when nothing has reminded you of your sister?
I’m not sure. It can just come on, I suppose… I don’t always notice what set it off.
Over the past month, have you been feeling hopeless?
I don’t know… hopeless is a strong word. I’ve felt low, but I’m not sure I’d call it that.
In the past month, have there still been moments when something could make you feel genuinely good, even briefly?

Sometimes, I suppose, but it feels… muted. I still go to book club, or the dance night, but I’m sort of just there. Like there’s glass between me and everyone. Even the garden, or cooking for the neighbors… it doesn’t give me that little lift like it used to.
During the past month, have you felt sad or down most of the day nearly every day?
I’m not sure I’d say most of the day, nearly every day. I have felt down… fairly often, I guess. It’s hard to pin down.

final_diagnosis.reason: Symptoms began about one month after the unexpected death of the patient's sister, a clear psychosocial stressor. The patient reports depressed mood, reduced pleasure, early-morning awakening, decreased appetite, guilt related to the death, and passive thoughts of death without plan. However, the interview did not clearly establish a full major depressive episode with depressed mood most of the day nearly every day, nor chronicity for dysthymia, nor recurrent episodes. The presentation is therefore most consistent with an adjustment disorder related to bereavement/stressor exposure.
